candidates.background: Libertarian nominee for Missouri's 1st Congressional District, running on a strict small-government platform: 'separation' of currency, healthcare and education from the state.

education.label: Backs 'separation of education and state'; 'all education must be privatized completely' (campaign site)

candidates.name: Robert Frank Onder Jr
candidates.background: Republican incumbent and physician representing eastern Missouri. Campaign site lists issue headings (immigration, taxes, elections, life) without elaboration; positions here combine those headings with his 2025 floor votes.

immigration.label: Lists 'Fighting illegal immigration' as a campaign priority; voted Yea on the Laken Riley Act, roll 23, Jan 22, 2025 (campaign site)

taxes.label: Lists 'cutting taxes' as a key policy goal; voted Aye on H.R. 1, the 2025 tax law, roll 190, Jul 3, 2025 (campaign site)

repro.label: Lists 'Defending Life' as a campaign priority, without further elaboration (campaign site)

democracy.label: Lists 'Securing Our Election' as a campaign priority, without further elaboration; did not vote (Not Voting) on the SAVE Act, roll 102, Apr 10, 2025 (campaign site)

health.label: Voted aye on H.R.1, the 2025 reconciliation law that cut federal Medicaid spending roughly $911B over 10 years via nationwide work requirements (clerk.house.gov roll 190, Jul 3, 2025)

climate.label: Voted yes on H.J.Res. 88, disapproving California's EPA waiver for its EV/clean-car sales mandate (clerk.house.gov roll 114, May 1, 2025)

safety.label: Voted yes on H.R.27/S.331, the HALT Fentanyl Act permanently classifying fentanyl analogues as Schedule I with mandatory minimums (clerk.house.gov roll 33, Feb 6, 2025)
